insider_note: The names are misleading and examiners know it: the CODING strand is the one that is NOT copied. Say that plainly.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Template strand
steps.margin_note: What it is, what is built from it, and its direction.
lines: During transcription the two strands of DNA
The TEMPLATE strand is the one that is actually
The mRNA is built complementary to it.
steps.why: The template is the strand the enzyme reads, so the RNA comes out complementary to it and identical to the other one.
common_mistakes: Saying the template strand is the same as the mRNA. The mRNA is COMPLEMENTARY to it.
Giving its direction as 5' to 3'. The template is read 3' to 5'.
steps.memory_tip: The template is read, not copied.

steps.label: Coding strand
steps.margin_note: Say it is not read, then explain why it is still called coding.

lines.text: The CODING strand is the one NOT read

lines: The CODING strand is the OTHER strand, which is
It is called the coding strand because its

steps.why: The strand that codes for nothing is called the coding strand precisely because it matches the message — a name that describes the sequence, not the job.
common_mistakes: Saying the coding strand is transcribed. It is NOT read at all.
Not explaining the name. The name is the confusing part and explaining it is the mark.
steps.memory_tip: The coding strand does no work; it just matches the message.
